styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Terracotta Army, city walls and the old capital's relics.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Muslim Quarter snacks, dumplings and hand-pulled noodles.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Pagodas, temples, calligraphy streets and Tang-era shows.

stays.why: Central and walkable. Close to the Bell and Drum Towers, the Muslim Quarter and metro lines.
Quieter old-town lanes near the wall and the calligraphy street. Good for evening walks.
Near the pagoda, museums and the fountain square. Lively at night, a bit south of the walls.
Best for early high-speed trains. Few sights nearby; use the metro to reach the center.

food: Eat in the Muslim Quarter: roujiamo (meat sandwich), yangrou paomo (lamb soup with bread) and grilled skewers. Prices are low; check the bill.
Try biangbiang noodles and hand-pulled noodles at small local shops. A bowl is often ¥15–35.
Dumpling banquets are a Xi'an classic. Book ahead for dinner shows; expect ¥80–200 per person.
Breakfast like a local: jinggao, hulatang (pepper soup) and sesame flatbreads from street stalls.
Tap water is not for drinking. Drink bottled or boiled water, and be careful with very spicy or cold street food if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Add a half day at the Shaanxi History Museum (book free tickets online in advance) and the Big Wild Goose Pagoda area.
Take a day trip to Mount Huashan by high-speed train for cable-car views; check weather and train times on the day.
Spend an evening at the Tang Paradise or a Tang-dynasty dinner show, or cycle the full city wall loop (rental about ¥45).

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Terracotta Army, the city wall and the Muslim Quarter; add a night for museums and a day trip.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 6°C and lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat; few rainy days.
February: still cold, highs near 10°C. Quiet sights and low prices.
March: warming to about 18°C. Good walking weather; a few rainy days.
April: mild and pleasant, highs near 23°C. One of the best months to visit.
May: warm at about 28°C. Comfortable mornings; book hotels early around holidays.
June: hot, highs near 31°C. Sightsee early and rest in the afternoon.
July: hottest month, highs near 33°C with about 10 rain days. Carry water and an umbrella.
August: hot and wet, similar to July. Plan indoor museums at midday.
September: cools to about 26°C. Pleasant and a good shoulder month.
October: mild at about 19°C. Great for the wall and outdoor sights.
November: cooler, highs near 13°C. Fewer crowds; bring layers.
December: cold, highs near 7°C and lows around -3°C. Dry and quiet.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold dry winters, hot humid summers with the most rain, and mild spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Mild days around 19–28°C. Ideal for the city wall, the Terracotta Army and walking the old town.

items.title: Summer is hot and wet (June to August)
items.text: Highs of 31–33°C with about 8–10 rain days a month. Go out early, carry water and an umbrella.

items.title: Winter is cold and dry
items.text: January highs near 6°C and lows around -4°C. Few rainy days; pack a warm coat and layers.

items.title: Rain peaks in late summer and autumn
items.text: About 10 rain days a month from July to October. Showers are often short; a light rain jacket helps.

items.title: Spring can be dusty
items.text: March to May sometimes brings dusty, hazy air. Check the air quality on the day if you have breathing issues.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers for cool mornings, sunscreen and a hat in summer, a warm coat in winter.

transit.best: Metro for most sights; walk or bike inside the city walls.

modes.text: 12+ lines, single ride about ¥5. Buy a Changantong card or scan WeChat/Alipay. Fast and cheap for the station and main sights.
¥1–2 flat fare. Line 610 (tourist 8) links the station, Bell Tower and pagodas.
Taxis are cheap but hard to hail at rush hour and shift change; watch the meter. DiDi, WeChat and Alipay ride-hailing work widely.
Not advised for visitors. Traffic and parking are tough.
Best inside the city walls. Shared bikes are handy for the wall and short hops.
